paragraphs: This position combines clinical assessment with appliance design: verifying prescriptions, measuring the body, fitting orthoses or prostheses, and recording function and comfort; it is not suited to those who only want pure equipment manufacturing.
A fit signal is being willing to measure repeatedly, listen to patient feedback, and re-adjust and ask the team to review when fit or use problems arise.
The safety focus is skin pressure, pain, gait, and appliance damage; anomalies must stop the affected step and be handed to authorized clinical personnel per organizational procedures.

A fictional case can be used for a paper exercise: list the checklists for measurement, design, fitting, review, and patient guidance; the exercise cannot be treated as permission to work with real patients.

Core tasks include interviewing and measuring patients, designing appliances based on prescriptions, selecting materials, fabricating or supervising fabrication, fitting and adjusting, and checking fit, function, and comfort.
Alternates between medical settings and fabrication laboratories, including intake measurement, appliance fitting, and team communication.

A service cycle starts with verifying the prescription and goals, proceeds through measurement, design, fabrication, fitting, functional observation, and adjustment, and then moves to use instruction and follow-up.
Review of fit, function, comfort, and patient feedback.
O*NET tasks also include appliance repair and supervising fabrication, but patient prescriptions, clinical fit, and safety judgment cannot be equated with general mechanical repair.
The U.S. BLS describes it as usually requiring a master's degree and residency-style training, with some states also requiring licensure; specific conditions are verified by state and position.

Chinese position titles, qualifications, and services that medical institutions may provide require separate verification, and practice authority cannot be inferred from U.S. certification or this page's text.

Compared with medical appliance technicians, orthotists and prosthetists take on patient assessment, prescription collaboration, fitting, and follow-up; technicians focus on fabrication, processing, or repair.
Compared with physical therapists, both may collaborate in observing walking and function, but orthotists and prosthetists focus on the design and fitting of individualized appliances.
Compared with podiatrists, appliance fitting and the physician diagnosis and management of foot disease differ; the specific prescribing and treatment authority is verified by jurisdiction.

Medical appliance technicians focus on processing, fabrication, and repair; orthotists and prosthetists also directly assess patients and participate in prescription collaboration, fitting, and follow-up.

If you prefer material processing and manufacturing processes, you can learn about medical appliance technicians; if you want to take on patient assessment and appliance fitting responsibility, verify this occupation's formal training.
Digital scanning can assist with capturing shape; clinical personnel must verify posture, soft tissue, weight bearing, and the original measurements.
CAD can assist with modeling and component selection; prescription goals, alignment, and material applicability still require professional review.

Digital fabrication or 3D printing is a candidate fabrication method, and shorter working hours cannot be asserted from the occupational technology list; specific materials, finished-product strength, fit, and safety require separate verification of the process and professional fitting, and cannot be released by automated design.
Tools can organize patient records and adjustment history; privacy, identity, and versions must be verified.
AI can prompt appliance design changes but cannot replace judgment about pain, pressure sores, gait, and functional feedback.
Patient explanations can be drafted by tools first; authorized personnel must verify the use and care instructions.
A technology list does not equal organizational adoption rate and cannot be used to calculate job replacement probability.
Key human control points include prescription verification, fitting release, anomaly escalation, and follow-up responsibility handover.

Insufficient evidence: a nationwide comparable median, percentile, and starting pay for Chinese orthotists and prosthetists was not obtained. In 2025, medical employer health and social work was 146,266 for non-private and 75,631 for private, and manufacturing enterprise manufacturing was 113,594 for non-private and 76,055 for private, all in yuan as pre-tax annual averages. The industries include other positions and are not this occupation's wage or an individual range; excludes self-employment profits, and pure sales and research employers require separate verification.
When verifying Chinese job postings, distinguish actual positions such as clinical assessment and fitting, rehabilitation engineering, appliance fabrication, and sales service.
Region, institution, qualifications, patient population, on-site duties, and performance systems differ, and a single job offer cannot be written as a national median.
Keep the job posting, date, and duties, then compare pre-tax and post-tax, base and performance pay, and working hours.
The current U.S. BLS OOH edition shows this precise occupation's May 2025 median annual wage of $81,110; it is a national occupational statistic, not entry-level pay or an individual offer.
The lowest 10% given by BLS is below $46,350 and the highest 10% is above $119,810; the two ends are boundaries and do not equal the 25th or 75th percentile.

Industry wages change; for example, the federal government, medical equipment manufacturing, outpatient services, and hospitals have different medians and cannot be directly applied to a given employer.

The 2025 U.S. 29-2091 precise annual wage 25th percentile is 61,290 U.S. dollars and the 75th percentile is 99,990 U.S. dollars, from this round's O*NET wage table; they share the same basis as the 10th percentile 46,350, median 81,110, and 90th percentile 119,810, and are not interpolated from the known endpoints. Percentiles are not seniority levels, starting pay, or individual offers.

Over 2025—2035 the U.S. precise 29-2091 grows 12.9% overall (OOH rounds to 13%), with an official net increase of 1,200 people and annual average openings of 700 including replacements; 2025 employment of 9,500 rising to 10,700 in 2035. The O*NET old 2024—2034 employment trend is treated separately as history, not mixed by period, and does not infer AI adoption replacement, individual unemployment, or Chinese demand.
U.S. wages cannot be converted into Chinese occupational wages and do not prove that Chinese positions are completely equivalent to the U.S. occupational identity.

Editorial exploration suggestion; the predictive or comparative validity of this assessment for the occupation has not been verified.
Real patient services must meet local qualifications and organizational authorization; the following are editorial risk scenarios.
Verify identity and prescription, measurement conditions, skin and pain, material connections, wear instructions, and digital design review in sequence.

O*NET supports only the task and work context background; the following consequences, controls, and escalations are editorial suggestions and do not indicate risk probability or uniform legal requirements.
Patients and prescription and measurement personnel
May cause the appliance object or site to be mismatched.
The current U.S. BLS edition describes usually requiring an orthotics and prosthetics related master's program and completion of residency-style clinical training; some states require licensure.

First learn anatomy, biomechanics, materials, and patient communication; verify program accreditation and prerequisites before applying. Problem statement: fictional Y01 prescription says left side model A and the measurement page says right side model A; for Z01 the side and model agree, the fitting feedback records pain, but the summary writes comfortable and the review is blank. Paper rule: records must agree, feedback must not be deleted, and unknown does not equal acceptable. List the contradictions and persons to verify for both cases, and do not decide appliances or patient plans.
Practice assessment, casting, design, and appliance fabrication in a formal program, and real patient contact must be supervised.

Residency-style training connects assessment, fitting, and follow-up, keeping supervisory feedback and patient safety records. Reference: Y01 keeps the original prescription and measurement values, marks the left/right contradiction, and hands it to the original record's responsible person for verification, without changing the side; for Z01, keep the pain feedback, mark the comfortable summary contradiction and the blank review as pending authorized verification, and do not mark release or judge the cause. The work submits a two-line discrepancy verification table and a simulated transfer draft, listing the original values, unknowns, responsible person to verify, and correction records; it is not real fitting or diagnosis and treatment.
Certification or state licensure requirements may vary by region and position, and the certifying body and official state rules should be checked.
A portfolio can use fictional cases to show prescription goals, measurement plans, design trade-offs, fitting checks, and anomaly escalation; unauthorized patient data must not be used.

Chinese job hunting requires independently verifying the position title, statutory qualifications, medical institution division of labor, and responsible person, and the U.S. path cannot be transplanted directly.

On-the-job development relies on appliance quality, patient functional feedback, continuing education, and cross-team review. Seven days: Day 1 copy the Y/Z inputs and paper rules; Days 2—3 build the two-line table for left/right, model, feedback, and review; Days 4—5 write the pending-verification transfer draft that keeps the original values; Days 6—7 submit the table, draft, and simulated review feedback and correction records. Unverified items remain unresolved, no real patient data is used, and the side is not changed, nor are appliances adjusted or treatment carried out.

career_risk_cards.heading: Appliance fitting and patient safety risks

risks.mitigation: Verify the original prescription and identifiers, and hand contradictions to the responsible person for review.
risks.scenario: The prescription says left while the measurement says right, yet it is still used for fabrication.
risks.title: Identity and prescription mismatch

risks.affected_roles: Patients and measurement and design personnel
risks.consequence: May make appliance dimensions inconsistent with actual needs.
risks.mitigation: Keep the original condition values, and have trained personnel re-measure and record.
risks.scenario: Dimensions from different postures or loading are treated as the same condition.
risks.title: Measurement error

risks.consequence: May delay assessment of skin or fit problems.
risks.mitigation: Keep patient feedback, and pause the affected step and escalate per organizational procedures.
risks.scenario: The patient reports pain while the fitting summary writes comfortable.
risks.title: Skin pressure injury and pain

risks.affected_roles: Patients and the fabrication and release team
risks.consequence: May cause appliance failure and injury during use.
risks.mitigation: Complete the applicable quality checks, and unresolved items are not released by the tool.
risks.scenario: Unresolved missing items in material, connector, or finished-product checks are still released.
risks.title: Material or connector failure

risks.consequence: May increase misuse, falls, or care risks.
risks.mitigation: Authorized personnel verify the instructions, confirm understanding, and arrange follow-up.
risks.scenario: The patient misunderstands the wear and care instructions with no feedback channel.
risks.title: Falls and misuse

risks.affected_roles: Patients and tool users and reviewers
risks.consequence: May overlook individual loading, fit, and safety conditions.
risks.mitigation: Authorized personnel verify material alignment and patient feedback and keep the reasons for modifications.
risks.scenario: Automated design output is not reviewed against the prescription, original measurements, and on-site fitting.
risks.title: Tool output misjudgment
